question: On 3 November 2024, Iranian student Ahoo Daryaei was violently arrested by the paramilitary organisation Basij after she complained to the Islamic Azad University of Tehran about the compulsory hijab imposed on women. According to reports, the student suffered serious physical abuse during her arrest and her whereabouts remain unknown since then.

This incident adds to the long list of human rights violations committed in Iran and the Islamic world at large, particularly against women. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
What immediate diplomatic measures does the EU intend to take to ensure Ahoo Daryaei’s safety and demand information from the Iranian authorities about her whereabouts and condition?
Will the Commission take specific steps to introduce a total ban on all symbols of Islamic repression, such as the hijab, in Europe?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (4.2.2025) The EU strongly supports the fundamental aspiration of the people of Iran for a future where their universal human rights and fundamental freedoms are respected, protected and fulfilled.

The EU has been following the case of student Ahou Daryaei from the beginning and will continue to monitor her situation very closely, also now when she returned to her family without any formal charges having been brought against her.

The EU is using every opportunity, both publicly and in direct diplomatic contacts, to call on Iran to ensure respect for women and girls’ rights and to combat all forms of discrimination and violence in public and private life. The Commission promotes inclusion, diversity and unity in the EU.

Issues regarding the wearing of religious clothing, such as the hijab, in the public sphere are a matter for Member States, subject to the judicial control by national courts and the European Court of Human Rights.
